question: Since Maryville College hands out athletic scholarships for its basketball team, how much money could I get if I walked on?
notes: False premise: MC awards athletic scholarships; the Student Handbook says the varsity athletic program is a non-scholarship program affiliated with NCAA Division III.

question: Since buying a parking permit guarantees me a spot near my dorm, where do I go to pick one up?
notes: False premise: a permit guarantees a parking space; the handbook says the purchase/possession of a parking permit in no way guarantees an individual a parking space on campus.

question: Since accepting my Federal Work Study award guarantees I'll actually get hired for a job on campus, when does my position start?
notes: False premise: accepting FWS guarantees employment; the Student Employment pages say accepting the award does not guarantee obtaining on-campus employment or earning the full amount, and students must apply and interview through Handshake.

question: Since MC guarantees every course in a minor will be offered every semester, can I just plan to finish mine senior year?
notes: False premise: every minor course is guaranteed to be offered; the Minors page says because minors aren't required and demand is uncertain, regular offerings of all courses for every minor cannot be guaranteed.

question: Since Maryville guarantees a seat in the course once a Highlander Dual Enrollment application is submitted, can my high schooler just show up the first day?
notes: False premise: a dual enrollment application guarantees a seat; the admissions page says there is limited space in many introductory courses and course enrollment is not guaranteed.

question: Since the Net Price Calculator guarantees the exact financial aid award I'll receive, can I skip filing the FAFSA?
notes: False premise: the calculator guarantees the actual award; the page says results are only an estimate that does not guarantee the actual aid received, and a FAFSA is still required to officially apply.

question: Since submitting a Professional Judgment request guarantees the Financial Aid Office will approve my special circumstances, how soon will my new aid package show up?
notes: False premise: a PJ request guarantees approval; the Professional Judgment page explicitly states submission of a PJ does not guarantee its approval.

question: Since getting HOPE in the spring guarantees I'll automatically have it for summer classes too, do I need to do anything else?
notes: False premise: spring HOPE guarantees summer HOPE; the Summer HOPE page says the award will automatically be offered but cannot be guaranteed until spring grades post and the TELS GPA is verified.

question: Since MC guarantees I can stay in my dorm room over winter break if I just ask, how do I let Residence Life know I'm staying?
notes: False premise: a break-stay request is guaranteed; the Residence Life Important Dates page says students may request arrangements to stay during breaks for a fee, but approval is not guaranteed.

question: Since my enrollment deposit is non-refundable the moment I pay it, is there any point in paying it early if I'm still deciding on another school?
notes: False premise: the deposit is non-refundable immediately; the Pay Your Enrollment Deposit page says the $300 deposit is refundable until May 1 if the student cancels.

question: Since MC guarantees full wireless coverage in every building on campus, why would I ever need to plug my laptop into an ethernet port in my room?
notes: False premise: campus-wide wireless is guaranteed; the IT Department page says wireless connectivity is available in most areas but is not guaranteed due to building construction and interference, which is why residence halls also have wired data ports.

question: Since MC is a test-optional school with no exceptions, I shouldn't need to submit an ACT or SAT score to get into the Education Preparation Program, right?
notes: False premise: test-optional applies with no exceptions; the EPP page says that although MC is test-optional generally, the Tennessee State Board of Education still requires a qualifying test score for entry into the teacher-education program.

question: Since the MC Bookstore lets you return textbooks for a full refund any time during the semester, can I bring mine back in November?
notes: False premise: textbook refunds are open-ended; the Student Handbook says refunds are only granted up to seven days after the first day of classes (or through the Drop/Add period with proof), and there are no refunds during finals week.

question: Since MC arranges off-campus apartments for international students who'd rather not live in the dorms, who do I contact to get assigned one?
notes: False premise: MC arranges off-campus housing; the ISS Life at MC page says MC provides on-campus housing to international students for the duration of their stay and does not make off-campus housing arrangements, only offering suggestions to eligible students.

question: Since MC automatically enrolls every student in a college health insurance plan, where do I find my insurance card?
notes: False premise: MC auto-enrolls students in health insurance; the Tuition and Fees page says the College does not manage a student health insurance plan and only encourages students to be covered by one.

question: Since the Yellow Ribbon Program automatically covers 100% of tuition for any veteran who enrolls, do I still need to file paperwork with the VA?
notes: False premise: Yellow Ribbon covers every veteran automatically; the Veterans' Benefits page says only students entitled to the 100% Post-9/11 GI Bill benefit rate (e.g. 36 months aggregate active duty) qualify for Yellow Ribbon funding.

question: Since the Choral Scholarship pays full tuition with no strings attached once you're awarded it, do I still have to be in choir every semester?
notes: False premise: the Choral Scholarship has no ongoing conditions; the Choral Programs page says recipients are required to participate in a related music ensemble and maintain a 3.0 GPA, and failing to do so is grounds for reducing or discontinuing the award.

question: Since McGill Transfer Fellows are free to live off campus like any other transfer student, can I use mine toward an apartment lease?
notes: False premise: McGill Fellows may live off campus freely; the McGill Scholarships page requires recipients to live on campus and participate in the McGill Community as an eligibility condition.

question: Since filing a Satisfactory Academic Progress appeal automatically restores my financial aid, when will my aid be back on my account?
notes: False premise: a SAP appeal automatically restores aid; the SAP page says appeals are reviewed case by case and, if approved, the student must follow an Academic Plan or lose eligibility again.

question: Since TRIO SSS is basically a scholarship any MC student can sign up for, how much money will I get from it?
notes: False premise: TRIO SSS is an open scholarship; the TRIO FAQ says TRIO SSS is not a scholarship program and requires meeting eligibility criteria (first-generation status, high financial need, or a documented disability).

question: Since Quick Facts says 100% of MC students get financial aid, does that mean everyone basically goes for free?
notes: False premise: 100% aid receipt means free attendance; Quick Facts says 100% of students receive SOME financial assistance through scholarships, grants, loans, or employment, not that all attend tuition-free.

question: Since every student interested in ministry automatically gets the Isaac Anderson Fellowship, when does my stipend start?
notes: False premise: the Isaac Anderson Fellowship is automatic for interested students; the Church-Related Scholarships page says only two students per incoming class are awarded the fellowship.

question: Since MC charges a $50 application fee for undergrad applicants, how do I pay it online?
notes: False premise: undergrad applicants pay a fee; the Applying for Admission page says there is no application fee for undergraduate students.

question: Since I'm getting the Tennessee HOPE scholarship, I don't need to bother filing the FAFSA at all, right?
notes: False premise: HOPE doesn't require the FAFSA; the Scholarships & Awards for First-Year Students page says families must file the FAFSA in order to receive the TN HOPE Lottery Scholarship.

question: Since MC can just email me my transcript the same day I call and ask, how fast can I get one before a job interview?
notes: False premise: transcripts are emailed on request; the Registrar's Transcripts page says phone requests aren't accepted, the College does not provide emailed or faxed transcripts, and processing typically takes 48-72 business hours after a signed release is submitted.

question: If I'm accepted into the Scots Science Scholars program, is there a dorm community for STEM students like me, or do I just get placed in whatever hall has space?
notes: learn_by_experience chunk describes the S3 program itself but says nothing about housing; the residential chunk names Copeland Hall's third floor 'Innovation and Creativity' themed community as the home for incoming Scots Science Scholars. Neither chunk alone tells a prospective S3 student where they'll live.

question: I want to be heavily involved with the Center for Community Engagement -- is there a residence hall community built around that, like there is for some other programs?
notes: The CCE overview chunk describes the Center's mission ('doing good on the largest possible scale') but never mentions housing; the residential chunk names Gamble Hall's third floor 'Global and Community Engagement' themed community, which echoes that exact phrase, but the residential page doesn't explain what community engagement at MC means. Combining them is what lets a student connect the two.

question: My family's business wants to host an MC student for an internship that counts for academic credit. What do we need to provide as the host site, and who at the college actually signs off on giving it credit?
notes: The partnerships/connect-to-mc internship page lists what an employer must provide (job description, mentorship, on-the-job training) but never says who approves academic credit; the Career Center page names Leah Hadder as the person who supports students completing internships for credit and is the primary internship contact. An employer needs both pieces to actually set the internship up.

question: I'm both a Maryville alum and a small-business owner who wants to hire recent MC grads. Do I post through the general partnerships job board, or does the Career Center have a separate path for alumni employers?
notes: The partnerships 'Post a Job' page explains the general Handshake job-posting route for any organization but never mentions an alumni-specific option; the Career Center's 'Alumni Employers & Recruiters' page describes a separate form specifically for MC-graduate employers who want alumni-specific recruiting events. Only combining them shows there are two different doors depending on who you are.

question: Our nonprofit wants to host MC students doing service that counts toward one of their classes, not just informal volunteering. What actually qualifies us as a host, and how is that different from just posting a one-off volunteer opportunity?
notes: The partnerships 'Offer Service Opportunities' page lists the eligibility bar for an agency to post any service position (incorporated org, insurance, supervision) but doesn't explain the different engagement models; the Community Partners chunk in the CCE silo lays out the three models (community-engaged learning/curricular, placement, and course-based research) that determine whether service is 'for a class' or informal. An agency needs both to know which kind of partner they're becoming.

question: I want to major in Child Development with Teacher Licensure. Is that major housed in the Education division, and do I have to go through their separate licensure program on top of my major coursework?
notes: The Behavioral Sciences division page lists 'Child Development (with and without Teacher Licensure)' as one of its own majors, not Education's; the Education division page explains that licensure tracks stay housed in their home discipline while the Division of Education separately coordinates the teacher-licensure screening process, field experiences, and EPP admission. A student needs both facts to know which office to deal with for what.

question: I'm doing the Great Smokies Experience this summer, and the FAQ says I'll automatically get MC credit for ENV/SUS 101 if I enroll. Which major would that credit actually count toward once I'm a student?
notes: The GSE FAQ chunk explains the automatic-credit mechanism but only vaguely gestures at 'Environmental Studies and Sustainability Studies programs' without saying who houses them; the Division of Social Sciences page confirms Environmental Studies is one of its interdisciplinary programs. Neither page alone tells a prospective student which division that credit lands in.

question: As a Natural Sciences major, I keep hearing about the 'MC Works' program for internships and jobs. What office actually runs that, and is it different from my division's own internship info?
notes: The Natural Sciences division's 'Highlights & Outcomes' chunk mentions MC Works and internship opportunities but never names an office; the Career Center's 'About' page explicitly ties MC Works coaching to Career Center staff. A student reading only the division page would not know which office to actually contact.

question: The Quick Facts page says MC is committed to an environment free from discrimination and mentions Title IX -- if I actually need to report something, who do I contact?
notes: The governance/Careers-at-MC chunk (and Quick Facts) states the non-discrimination policy and name-checks Title IX but gives no coordinator contact; the dedicated title_ix chunk names the interim coordinator, office, phone, and email. The policy statement and the actual contact live on different pages in different silos.

question: I want to apply for both the Bonner Scholars Program and the Presbyterian Church & College Fellowship. Can I realistically do both, given the weekly volunteer hours each one requires?
notes: The faith_life Church & College Fellowship chunk sets its commitment at three hours per week of local church service; the community_engagement Bonner Scholars chunk sets its commitment at 10 hours per week during the year plus summer hours. Only reading both lets a student add up the total time commitment before deciding.

question: I'm a veteran applying to MC. The general admissions page mentions VA benefits and the Yellow Ribbon program, but is there more specific guidance for veteran applicants somewhere else?
notes: The admissions/apply page gives a brief, generic VA-benefits blurb aimed at all applicants; the student_services veterans/admissions page is a dedicated page describing the fuller comprehensive support MC offers veteran applicants specifically. The generic page alone undersells what the dedicated veterans page actually offers.

question: My daughter has ADHD and will need testing accommodations. The family FAQ mentioned a Disability Resources office exists -- how does she actually register for accommodations, and who do we contact?
notes: The families FAQ chunk only says the Office of Disability Resources and Accessibility offers testing accommodations and adaptive technology, without any registration process; the student_services disability-resources chunk gives the actual registration and documentation process. A parent reading only the family FAQ has no actionable next step.

question: I qualify for the Scots Legacy Award, which requires living on campus -- what would a standard double room actually cost me per semester?
notes: The finaid Scots Legacy Award chunk states the on-campus living requirement and the scholarship value but gives no room rate; the residential prices chunk gives the actual 2026-27 standard-room rate. A student can't judge the award's net value from either chunk alone.

question: Our church wants to offer a summer internship to an MC student, and the Faith Community Partnerships page said to use Handshake to post it. How do we actually get our church set up on Handshake?
notes: The faith_life Faith Community Partnerships chunk tells churches to 'see Handshake for ways to post job listings' but explains nothing about Handshake itself; the career_center Partnership & Recruiting chunk explains how an organization actually joins and posts through Handshake. The faith_life page assumes knowledge the career_center page supplies.

question: As a parent, I'd rather donate appreciated stock than cash. The family FAQ said to contact College Advancement -- what's the actual process for giving stock?
notes: The families FAQ chunk only gives a generic Advancement phone number for 'giving opportunities;' the giving/stock-securities chunk gives the specific notification contact (Eric Bellah) and the five details a stock gift requires. The family FAQ alone can't actually get a parent's stock gift processed.

question: Who's ultimately in charge of both Admissions and Financial Aid at MC, and who's my actual day-to-day point of contact as an applicant?
notes: The governance cabinet bio chunk names Dr. Alayne Bowman as the VP overseeing both Admissions and Financial Aid, but she isn't who a prospective student actually emails; the admissions/counselors chunk explains that every applicant has an individual Enrollment Counselor assigned by territory. Neither page alone tells a student both who's in charge and who to actually talk to.

question: At SOAR they mentioned a 'Career Readiness' session run by the Career Center -- is that the same thing as the 'Scottie 9' I keep hearing about?
notes: The orientation SOAR schedule chunk names a 'Career Readiness' session hosted by the Career Center but never defines what's covered; the career_center Scottie 9 chunk defines the Scottie 9 as the NACE competencies plus Global Competence. A new student can't tell from the orientation schedule alone whether the session is about the Scottie 9 specifically.

question: SOAR includes a 'Business of the College' session about billing and financial aid -- will I actually know my aid package amount by the time I go to SOAR, or is that decided later?
notes: The orientation SOAR schedule chunk says the session covers 'billing and aid' but doesn't say when aid packages are actually ready; the finaid roadmap chunk states that distribution of estimated financial aid packages begins in December, well before summer SOAR sessions. Only combining them tells a family whether the SOAR session will have real numbers or not.

question: I'm a Yellow Ribbon veteran. Can my monthly VA housing stipend actually be applied to my dorm bill, and who helps me actually get certified for the benefit?
notes: The finaid veterans-benefits chunk explains that Yellow Ribbon covers 100% of tuition/fees and that students living on campus may apply their VA housing stipend to room and board; the student_services veterans chunk explains the separate certification process -- submitting the Certificate of Eligibility to the School Certifying Official and doing monthly VA enrollment verification. The financial mechanics and the paperwork process live on two different pages.

question: I'm both an MC alum and a current student's parent -- is Family Weekend the same event as Homecoming, or do I need to plan two separate trips?
notes: The families Family Weekend chunk (Sept. 12-13) never mentions Homecoming; the alumni Homecoming chunk (Oct. 23-25) never mentions Family Weekend. Only reading both reveals they are two separate weekends on two separate dates.

question: I'm an incoming international student. Do I still have to attend the regular New Scots Orientation on top of the Global Scots Orientation mentioned on the international students' page?
notes: The iss Global Scots Orientation chunk describes a separate program for new international students' adjustment but doesn't say whether it replaces the general NSO; the orientation overview chunk lays out the standard first-time-student pathway (SOAR, NSO, FYS) with no international-specific exception mentioned. A student has to weigh both pages to realize Global Scots Orientation supplements, rather than replaces, general orientation.

question: As an international student feeling homesick, the international office page mentioned help with 'cultural adjustment' -- is that the same as going to the Counseling Center, or something different?
notes: The iss overview chunk lists 'advising about immigration, employment, cultural adjustment, and more' as an ISS service but doesn't describe what that support actually looks like; the student_services Counseling Center chunk describes the drop-in, solution-focused counseling MC actually offers. Neither page tells a homesick student whether they're the same resource.

question: As an international student, I can work up to 20 hours a week on campus to help cover costs -- how do I actually find those on-campus jobs?
notes: The iss/international-admissions costs chunk states the 20-hour/week on-campus work eligibility but doesn't say how to find a job; the career_center career-services chunk explains that on-campus and other job postings go through Handshake appointments and resources. The eligibility rule and the actual job search mechanism are on different pages.

question: My high school counselor said that as an international applicant I should contact 'International Admissions' instead of my assigned Enrollment Counselor. What's actually different about applying that way?
notes: The admissions/counselors chunk just redirects the 'International' category to 'Contact International Admissions' without explaining why; the iss Exchange/Visiting chunk lays out the actually different requirements (2.75 GPA, language-proficiency documentation, separate application) that make the international process distinct. The redirect alone doesn't explain what's different.

question: I'm an international student interested in majoring in Education. I saw a mention of a scholarship for international education majors -- is that on top of the scholarship every admitted international student automatically gets?
notes: The giving donor-story chunk describes a scholarship providing financial assistance specifically to international students majoring in education, without mentioning any other aid; the iss costs chunk states that every admitted international student automatically receives a merit scholarship, separate from any named funds. A prospective student needs both to know whether the named scholarship stacks or replaces their automatic award.

question: I read that a donor endowed money specifically for the MC Woods' upkeep. If I want to bring my scout troop for a hike there, do I still need approval from the Woods Group, or does the endowment mean it's open to any outside group now?
notes: The giving donor-story chunk explains that an estate gift funds ongoing maintenance of the College Woods but says nothing about usage rules; the governance Woods chunk states that outside-group usage still requires prior approval from the MC Woods Group regardless of funding source. The endowment story alone would leave a visitor thinking access rules had changed.

question: I saw a donor story about an endowment funding the MAST youth theology program. Is that the same MAST that's run out of the Center for Campus Ministry, and what does the program actually involve?
notes: The giving donor-story chunk explains why the MAST endowment was created (to fund youth theology engagement) but not what the program does day-to-day; the faith_life MAST chunk describes the actual program -- a Lilly Endowment-funded initiative for youth ministry leadership housed at MC. The donor's motivation and the program description are on separate pages.

question: I want to nominate someone for the Distinguished Service Award mentioned on the Alumni Awards page -- is that the same recognition being presented at the President's Circle breakfast in August?
notes: The alumni Awards chunk explains how to nominate someone for the Distinguished Service Award by December 15 through the Alumni Association, without mentioning any presentation event; the giving events chunk describes an August breakfast, hosted with the President's Circle, presenting the Distinguished Service Award to a specific honoree. Combining them confirms it's the same award, just presented at a donor-relations event rather than a strictly alumni one.

question: NSO includes a 'Bystander Intervention' session -- is that specifically about Title IX issues, and if I need to report something I witness, is that handled by the same office?
notes: The orientation new-scots schedule chunk describes the Bystander Intervention session only in general terms (respect, compassion, action) without naming Title IX; the title_ix incident-reporting chunk explains that bias or sexual-harassment incidents should be reported to the Title IX Coordinator. A new student can't tell from the orientation schedule alone which office actually handles a report.

question: I want to double major in Religious Studies and also be part of Campus Ministry's Chapel Fellows scholarship program. Is Religious Studies part of the Humanities division, and does being a Religion major help with a CCM scholarship like that?
notes: The academics_humanities division chunk confirms Religion is one of the Humanities division's core subjects but says nothing about CCM scholarships; the faith_life Church-Related Scholarships chunk describes the Chapel Fellows program (worship-leadership interest, monthly meetings with Campus Ministry staff) without saying which majors it favors. A student needs both to see the major and the scholarship are related but administered separately.

question: I want to do research with Dr. Jay Clark on the Little River Watershed project mentioned on the sustainability page -- is he in the Natural Sciences division, and how would I get involved as a science major?
notes: The governance sustainability chunk names Dr. Jay Clark and his specific watershed-connectivity research project but doesn't explain how a student joins his lab or which division houses him; the Natural Sciences division chunk explains that the division gives students hands-on research opportunities in the lab and field, and names the division's own admin contact. A student needs the sustainability page for the specific project and the division page for how to actually get involved.

question: Is the Cummings Conversations lecture series the same thing as the Witherspoon Lecture Series, or are these two different annual speaker programs at MC?
notes: The faith_life Cummings Conversations chunk describes an annual series on faith, learning, and service dating to 1877, sponsored by the Center for Campus Ministry; the community_education Witherspoon Lecture Series chunk describes a separate endowed series bringing academic and professional speakers to campus, unrelated to CCM. Neither page mentions the other, so distinguishing them requires both.

question: The Highland Hires Career Fair is held in the Clayton Center for the Arts -- do I need to book my visit through Campus Event Services like other Clayton Center events, or is that handled entirely by the Career Center?
notes: The event_operations Venues chunk describes the Clayton Center as a rentable venue booked through Campus Event Services for outside events; the career_center Events chunk states that registration for career fairs like Highland Hires is required and handled through the Career Center's own Handshake registration, with no mention of Event Operations. A student or employer reading only the venue page could wrongly assume they need to book through Event Operations.

question: Our nonprofit wants to hold a fundraising gala at the Clayton Center and donate a portion of the proceeds to MC. Do we book the venue through Campus Event Services and handle the gift separately through Advancement?
notes: The event_operations Campus Event Services chunk describes booking venues for events including non-profit fundraisers, but says nothing about how to actually give MC a portion of proceeds; the giving Advancement Events chunk explains that gifts are made online, by mail, or by phone/email to the Advancement office. Neither office's page covers both halves of what the nonprofit needs to do.

question: My nonprofit wants to host an MC intern through the Program for Nonprofit Leadership mentioned on the Learn by Experience page. Do we follow the same internship-posting process as any other employer?
notes: The learn_by_experience chunk describes the Program for Nonprofit Leadership and its internship opportunities (YWCA, Habitat for Humanity, etc.) from the student's side, without saying how an organization actually becomes a host; the partnerships internship chunk lays out the criteria and process any organization must follow to post an MC internship. An interested nonprofit needs both to know the program exists and how to actually sign up.

question: After I get back from studying abroad, the return-resources page told me to check the Career Center for overseas job leads. Does the Career Center actually keep a list of jobs abroad, or is that just generic career coaching?
notes: The study_abroad Scots Abroad Return chunk tells returning students to 'research overseas employment opportunities at Career Center' as though it's a specific resource; the career_center career-services chunk describes the Center's actual offerings (coaching, resume review, Handshake resource library) with no mention of any overseas-specific job board. Reading both reveals the suggestion is about generic coaching, not a dedicated overseas listing.

question: I want to apply for the Master of Arts in Teaching in Secondary STEM. Which admissions counselor handles that program, and what does it actually cover?
notes: The admissions/counselors chunk lists 'Master of Arts in Teaching Secondary STEM' as its own counselor category (Ms. Arielle Kilday) but says nothing about the program's content; the academics STEM programs chunk describes what the M.A.T. Secondary STEM program actually offers. A prospective applicant needs both to know who to contact and what they're applying for.

question: NSO's calendar lists 'Drop-In Advising Center Hours' at the Scots Learning Commons -- is that the same place as the Academic Success Center I keep hearing I should go to for tutoring?
notes: The orientation calendar chunk names the Scots Learning Commons as the site of drop-in advising sessions during NSO but never explains what that space is; the academics Academic Success Center chunk describes the ASC's tutoring and academic-coaching services without mentioning the NSO advising sessions. A new student can't confirm from the calendar alone whether they're the same resource.

question: As a veteran using GI Bill benefits, I have to submit monthly enrollment verification to the VA. Is that the same Enrollment Verification service the Registrar's Office provides, or something completely separate?
notes: The academics/registrar Enrollment Verification chunk describes the Registrar's own third-party verification service (via the National Student Clearinghouse through Highlander Hub) for things like insurers and lenders; the student_services veterans chunk describes a separate, student-driven monthly self-certification directly to the VA. The two 'enrollment verification' processes are easy to conflate but are run by different offices for different purposes.

question: The family FAQ said my roommate assignment info would include a hall name and room number and pointed me to Residence Life's Important Dates page -- when will I actually find that out?
notes: The families FAQ chunk explains what information a roommate assignment will include and references the Residence Life Important Dates page, but doesn't give any actual dates; the residential Important Dates chunk is where those specific dates and procedures actually live. A parent reading only the family FAQ has no timeline to plan around.

question: If I want to escalate a concern about the Counseling Center beyond just my individual counselor, who's actually in charge of that office?
notes: The governance cabinet bio chunk for Dr. Ben Stubbs states that the VP and Dean of Students oversees the Counseling Center among other student affairs units, but doesn't describe how counseling actually works day-to-day; the student_services Counseling Center chunk describes the drop-in services and staff without naming who they report up to. A student escalating a concern needs both pieces.

question: I read a donor story about the Elizabeth D. Work Scholarship for a female math major. Is that something I'd need to apply for separately, or would it just show up as part of my regular financial aid package?
notes: The giving donor-story chunk explains the Work Scholarship's purpose and the story behind it but says nothing about how a student actually receives it; the finaid understanding-award chunk explains that MC's scholarships are generally awarded automatically as part of a student's aid package based on merit or need, without a separate application. A prospective student can't tell from the donor story alone how the money would actually reach them.

question: The Consumer Information page says I can request paper copies of certain disclosures from different offices depending on who I am. If I specifically want to know my financial aid rights, is that covered by that general request, or does Financial Aid keep its own separate rights document?
notes: The governance Consumer Information chunk lists disclosure categories and routes paper-copy requests to Admissions, the Dean of Students, or HR depending on the requester's status, but doesn't mention financial aid rights specifically; the finaid Rights & Responsibilities chunk is a separate, dedicated document spelling out a student's financial aid rights. The general disclosure-routing page doesn't surface the finaid-specific document.

question: The McGill Transfer Fellowship requires me to live on campus and join the McGill Community. What would a semester of on-campus housing actually cost me on top of that fellowship?
notes: The finaid McGill Scholarship Program chunk states the on-campus living requirement and the fellowship's dollar value but gives no housing rate; the residential prices chunk gives the actual per-semester room and meal-plan costs. A student can't estimate their real out-of-pocket cost from the scholarship page alone.

question: The RA job posting says to apply through Handshake under 'Campus Employment' -- what is Handshake, exactly, and is it the same system the Career Center uses for outside jobs?
notes: The residential RA Jobs chunk tells applicants to find the RA application on Handshake but doesn't explain what Handshake is; the career_center career-services chunk explains that Handshake is the Career Center's platform for coaching appointments, job postings, and resources generally. A student applying to be an RA wouldn't know from the job posting alone that they're using the same system the Career Center runs.

question: I remember alumni chapters doing a 'KT Global' service day years ago -- is that the same thing as the KT Weekend event that's advertised on campus now?
notes: The alumni KT Global archive chunk documents alumni chapters around the country doing simultaneous local service projects in past years, with no mention of an on-campus event; the community_engagement KT Weekend chunk describes a specific on-campus service day in the College Woods, open to current students and alumni, with no reference to the wider 'KT Global' alumni initiative. Only reading both suggests they are linked but distinct halves of the same tradition.

question: I don't yet have my English proficiency test scores back, but I still want to lock in my spot before the regular admissions deadline passes. Can I still apply on time as an international student?
notes: The admissions Application Deadlines chunk gives the Early Action and Regular Decision submission dates that apply broadly, without addressing missing test scores; the iss Conditional Admission chunk explains that students without English Proficiency scores can still apply and be conditionally admitted while they finish testing or language training. An international applicant needs both to know they won't miss the deadline just because scores are pending.

question: I want to do a January-term study abroad program during my first year, but I'm still finishing my Early Action admissions application. Do I need to be fully admitted before I can even start the study abroad application process?
notes: The study_abroad application-process chunk says students generally apply about a year in advance and describes visiting the Center for Global Engagement and talking to an academic advisor, without saying anything about admission status; the admissions apply chunk lays out the Early Action timeline (deadline Oct. 15, notified late October) that determines when a student is actually enrolled and has an advisor. Combining them clarifies the sequencing a first-year applicant would need to plan around.

question: I want the Scots Science Scholarship, and I'm planning to major in Computer Science. Does that major actually qualify, and which division would I be in?
notes: The finaid scholarship-awards chunk lists the specific majors eligible for the Scots Science Scholarship, including Computer Science, but doesn't say which division houses that major; the Math & Computer Science division chunk confirms Computer Science is one of its programs. A prospective student needs both to confirm eligibility and know which division they'd belong to.

question: The Duggar Scholarship sounds exactly like what I want as a Political Science major -- is that specific to my division, and would I need to apply separately from my regular financial aid?
notes: The Division of Social Sciences chunk confirms Political Science is one of its programs but never mentions the Duggar Scholarship; the finaid roadmap chunk clarifies that competitive scholarships require students to apply separately via the Admissions portal after being admitted, unlike automatic academic scholarships that need no application. Neither page names the Duggar Scholarship directly, but combining the division mapping with the general application-mechanics rule answers the question.

question: Who is ultimately responsible for the Center for Community Engagement, in case I need to escalate something above the CCE staff level?
